title: AI Research Assistant for Clinical Trials
AI Research Assistant for Clinical Trials
AI Research Assistant for Clinical Trials
text:
How it works
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) means a language model first retrieves relevant documents, then generates an answer from them. Here, the documents are 12,000+ clinical trials running in Australia. Each question goes through six steps:

Understand the question. A language model turns the question into search terms: diseases, drugs and their other names, and filters such as status or sponsor.
Find the trials. SQL queries in DuckDB select the matching trials, and embeddings rank them by how close their content is in meaning to the question.
Count. A SQL query counts which drugs appear across all matching trials.
Write. A language model writes a short answer from the top trials and the counts, citing a trial ID for each claim.
Check. A separate language model call compares each claim in the answer with the trials it cites, and removes anything they don’t support.
Answer. The final answer is presented, with each trial’s phase, status and sponsor taken directly from the trial records.

title: Food Delivery: An AI Agent for Ops Teams
text: This AI agent answers operations questions about 196,000 food deliveries from DoorDash’s publicly available data (early 2015). A language model reads each question and chooses a tool: for questions about past deliveries it writes and runs a SQL query; for questions about a new order it uses a delivery-time model I trained. It then explains the result in plain English.
